featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Muthuswamy Cafe, and it was an amazing experience for anyone who loves authentic South Indian food.

The place has a simple yet comforting vibe, and the aroma itself sets the mood as soon as you walk in. The food is absolutely top-notch—fresh, flavorful, and perfectly balanced. From crispy dosas to soft idlis and rich sambhar, everything tasted authentic and satisfying.

The service was quick and efficient, and the staff was polite and attentive throughout. It’s one of those places where you go for the food and end up loving the whole experience.

If you’re in Dadar and craving real South Indian flavors, this spot is definitely worth visiting!

featured_reviews.name: Himanshi Patel
featured_reviews.review_text: Café Muthuswami in Dadar is a cozy spot that brings authentic South Indian flavors to life. Known for its crispy dosas, soft idlis, and rich, aromatic filter coffee, every bite feels comforting and nostalgic. The ambiance is simple yet inviting, perfect for casual catch-ups or a relaxed solo meal. Service is quick, and the food quality is consistently impressive. Whether you’re craving a hearty breakfast or a light evening snack, this café delivers on both taste and experience. A must-visit for anyone who loves traditional South Indian food in Mumbai with a homely touch and great value.

featured_reviews.name: Pooja Fulsundar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mutuswami Cafe is located just outside Dadar East railway station, so it’s very easy to find and perfect for a quick stop after travel. They have both indoor and outdoor seating, which is nice if you want to sit comfortably or just grab something quickly.
We tried the strawberry milkshake & mango milkshake both were thick, chilled, and refreshing. The paper masala dosa was big, crispy, and came with good chutney and sambar. Kanchipuram idli was soft and flavourful, a little different from regular idli and worth trying.
Cheese tava rice was spicy, cheesy, and filling good if you’re very hungry. We ended with pineapple sheera, which was warm, slightly sweet, and had a nice fruity taste.
Overall, it’s a good place for South Indian food and quick snacks near the station.

featured_reviews.name: VISHAL UPADHYAY
featured_reviews.review_text: We ordered cheese pav bhaji, and masala dosa and both were extremely delicious. We loved both the items. Cost wise it appeared a little costly given the ambience, and quality of service. It was situated near Dadar railway station and is fine for some snacking.

featured_reviews.name: Gayatri
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re in Dadar and craving authentic South Indian flavors any time of the day, Muttuswami Cafe is the place to be!
This is the only café in the area open 24/7, making it a perfect spot for early breakfasts, late-night cravings, or casual meetups at any hour.
The food quality is outstanding, with every dish served fresh, flavorful, and satisfying:
Cheese Pav Bhaji – perfectly buttery with a generous layer of melted cheese that elevates the classic taste.
Podi Idli – soft, bite-sized idlis coated beautifully in spicy podi masala and ghee.
Muttuswami Special Benne Dosa – rich, crispy, and soaked in butter with a delicious traditional touch.
Spring Dosa – a unique fusion twist, crispy outside with a flavorful stuffed filling inside.
Fruit Custard Dessert – creamy, refreshing, and loaded with fresh fruits for the perfect sweet ending.
Their fresh juices are equally impressive — especially the pomegranate juice and the orange-mosambi mix, both refreshing and naturally sweet.
What truly makes the experience special is the warm and polite staff. The service is quick, attentive, and always delivered with a smile. The beautiful interiors create a clean, cozy, and welcoming atmosphere, making you want to sit back and enjoy your meal.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Arya Bhavan Run by Muthuswamy this Restaurant has opened in the recent past at Vile Parle east relatively new to western suburbs i have been eating at the OG Matunga outlet bang opp Matunga central Railway Station close to 2 decades now

1.This is the run and owned  by the same family who runs the matunga eatery since day one it opened in vile parle east i started frequenting this place  I must clearly point out my observations for this place
Food is not as perfected like the OG Arya bhavan at matunga i feel that  matunga  has good chefs and service staff to deliver Excellence this vile parle branch offers almost the same menu  but at  times I felt that the food goes haywire chutneys sometimes  are very  well prepared  but some times watery chutneys and half done dosas not done right.

2.i feel  owner should & MUST visit this place atleast 3 times a week though his son and the owner himself know me i feel the service and food here get wonky many  times as they have recently expanded to other branches in sewri chembur too hence staff issue remains a challenge in kitchen as well in service.

3.So the rating 3 is given in comparison with the Original Matunga Arya Bhavan the food otherwise is amazing rite from the masala dosa perfectly made to the Medu vada -is Must try make sure they freshly make it for you when u order it the best perfect medu vada i have ever eaten in mumbai (matunga branch does it right each time everytime) they serve the amazing red green thick freshly made chutneys and perfectly made Sambhar

Thathe idli with podi is perfect

Another hidden gem in the menu is Biscuit Dosa its heaven specially if u like pizzas u will like this Innovatively made dosa styled and made by them.

Idlis are well made nice fluffy perfected with their in-house spl batter u will notice the difference in the first bite itself

They have other variety of dosas like palak dosa Mysore dosa which go well select ur pick

Kanchipuram idli Brahman idli all are good

The best part is they have full ac Restaurant with table service

The service is wobbly which I have complained to the owner once as you have to keep asking people to clean table for water for your food to be served hence I rate service 2star as the staff training is a challenge here getting staff is a bigger challenge in this place hence if they have full strength of staff you might get proper service sometimes they will forget chutneys with dosas hence you will have to ask them for chutneys by the time they get chutney dosa will be over the person who cleans tables may not clean the table properly you may have to ask again for it constantly you will have to ask for water tissue spoon etc ....they may not be proactive it all depends on the staff mood so

While ac works fine washroom is a challenge to use as water soap tissues hygeine are clear issues which owner has to address ASAP

this place  is way above the average south indian Udupi restaurants and its can be termed as a gem for south indian breakfast lovers it does decent "ghati" desi style pizza too few sandwiches freshly made juices and has started chaats

Showstopper is the goti sodas with flavours ,Ananda milk is stocked up and has handmade ice cream which  could definitely be tried chocolate Orange my personal favorite

Coin idli ,butter idli, are all time favorite

Rassam wada is another gem in their menu but have it with pipping hot rasam  and freshly made vada

Their tomato Rasam served here is another favourite's I sometimes come here just to have that however matunga outlet  does it better

Filter coffee is decent served in traditional brass tumbler set with spl sugar

Parking is roadside avoid going on weekends public holidays

Must visit the place after 8.30am before noon on weekdays to avoid  any waiting reservation is not required they are there on swiggy zomato however eating food going there is recommended

Curd rice, bisse bille bhat pav bhaji all is served

Looking for variety seated service with ac  quality food  this is it!!

featured_reviews.name: Sagar Abichandani
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (4/5)

Ramashray in Matunga is one of those classic South Indian institutions that still feels properly “Bombay” – bustling, no-nonsense and absolutely focused on the food. I dropped in specifically to try their ghee podi Thatte idli and walked out very happy (and very full).

The ghee podi Thatte idli is easily the hero of the menu. The idli itself is thick and soft – that perfect Thatte style – with a beautiful fermented flavour. It comes drenched in ghee, with a generous ring of podi that clings to every bite. The texture, temperature and seasoning were spot on; this is the kind of dish you could reorder without thinking twice.

The pineapple sheera was another standout. Warm, fragrant and not cloyingly sweet, with enough pineapple to cut through the richness of ghee – it felt like a proper old-school dessert, the kind you’d expect from a place that’s been doing this for decades. If you have a sweet tooth, this is non-negotiable.

Where the experience dipped a bit for me was the masala dosa. For a place with Ramashray’s reputation, I expected a benchmark dosa, but it was underwhelming:
•	The dosa was small in size compared to typical Matunga standards.
•	The texture lacked crispness – instead of that satisfying crunch, the dosa kept crumbling even when handled gently, which made it messy and not very enjoyable.
•	The masala itself was decent, but the base failed to carry it.

Service is fast, efficient and very typical of old-school South Indian joints in Mumbai – you’re seated, served and cleared quickly, which works well given the constant rush. Prices are reasonable for the quality, and the overall vibe is nostalgic: crowded, lively, with conversations, steel plates and filter coffee aromas all blending into one.

Overall, Ramashray still deserves its cult status for certain dishes, especially the ghee podi Thatte idli and pineapple sheera, which I would come back for in a heartbeat. I’m giving it 4 stars only because the masala dosa – usually the litmus test at a South Indian eatery – fell short on texture and portion size. Fix that, and this would easily be a 5-star experience.

The Chicken Modak was the surprise star—moist chicken kheema wrapped in a soft, pillowy coating. Though, between us, it did look slightly jaundiced.

They ended the meal with complimentary Caramel Custard—light, soft, and just the right sweetness.

The staff were courteous and attentive, the ambience warm and welcoming.

Ambience: A+

What started as a quest for Poe and Pao turned into a delicious detour, a reminder that some of the best finds in Mumbai happen purely by serendipity.

We quickly ordered a few items — Idli Vada, Molgapodi Idli, Molgapodi Masala Dosa, Mysore Masala Dosa, along with beverages like Filter Coffee and Sugarcane Juice.

If you’re visiting Mumbai and searching for the best South Indian breakfast in Juhu, you cannot miss Benne Heritage Bangalore Dosa.

This place truly has a hype of its own — and after experiencing it firsthand, I can confidently say it deserves every bit of it.

As a North Indian, I had never even heard of a “Benne Dosa” before my trip. But the buzz around this spot was so strong among locals that I felt compelled to try it.

I arrived in the morning and ended up standing in line for nearly an hour just to get in — which might sound intense, but the experience began impressing me even before I entered. The staff personally came to people waiting in line, thanked us for our patience, and even offered sweets. That level of hospitality instantly set the tone and showed how much they value their customers.

Inside, the place is lively, energetic, and completely packed. This is not a traditional sit-down restaurant; most guests stand and eat, with designated tables only for elderly guests, pregnant women, small children, or those with medical conditions.

Ordering is fully digital through self-service screens — you select your items, pay, and receive a token. There’s also a glass-panel view of the kitchen so you can watch your food being freshly prepared, which adds to the authenticity and excitement. When your token appears, you collect your order downstairs and enjoy your meal.

On recommendation from regular customers there, I ordered the Benne Plain Dosa, Benne Masala Dosa, Donne Biryani, and Cold filter Coffee — and honestly, this turned out to be the most heavenly South Indian meal I’ve ever had anywhere, whether in India or abroad. The flavors were outstanding, the texture perfect, and every bite felt worth the wait. The iced filter coffee alone is reason enough to visit.

Final verdict: If you love authentic South Indian food or are a food tourist exploring Mumbai, this place is an absolute must-visit.

Long queue or not, I would gladly wait again just to relive this meal. Without a doubt, this is my favorite South Indian food spot on earth so far.

featured_reviews.review_text:
If comfort food had a personality, it would probably be Benne in Juhu. Benne - Heritage Bangalore Dosa has mastered the art of making South Indian food feel indulgent, nostalgic, and ridiculously satisfying all at once.

The star of the meal for me was easily the thatte idli - soft, fluffy, drenched in ghee, coated generously with podi masala, and honestly the kind of dish that instantly hits the spot. Every bite felt rich, comforting, and packed with flavour without trying too hard.

The dosas here deserve all the hype they’ve been getting across Mumbai food circles. I tried the Benne plain dosa, masala dosa, podi masala dosa, and garlic dosa - and somehow each one had a completely different personality. Crisp edges, buttery centres, perfect fermentation, and that signature Bangalore-style benne flavour that keeps lingering long after the meal ends. The chutneys deserve their own fanbase honestly - fresh, balanced, and addictive enough to want extra servings every single time.

The medu vadas were another standout - beautifully crisp on the outside, soft and airy inside, exactly how a good vada should be. And then came the filter coffee ice cream from their collab with Indu Ice Creams, which genuinely felt like the perfect ending to the meal. Creamy, strong coffee notes, slightly nostalgic, and an absolute must-try.

The space itself has a very minimal yet aesthetic South Indian café vibe - warm lighting, clean interiors, subtle Bangalore darshini-inspired energy, and an atmosphere that somehow feels both trendy and comforting together. A lot of diners online consistently rave about the crispy dosas, fresh chutneys, and ambience, and after visiting, it’s very easy to understand the obsession.

Overall, Benne feels less like just another dosa place and more like a love letter to Bangalore-style comfort food - buttery, soulful, and dangerously addictive.

The filter coffee was served strong—maybe a bit too strong for my liking—so if you prefer a milder coffee, that’s something to keep in mind.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Mani’s Lunch Home-
Since 2007, during my monthly early morning office tours, I make it a personal ritual to stop at Mani’s Lunch Home in Matunga East for breakfast. No matter how early the day begins or how packed the schedule looks, I always get down here first—it’s my way of starting the day on the right note.
Over the years, I’ve tasted nearly every item served here. But my usual favorites are the idli-vada, medu vada, and the classic sada dosa. The idlis are soft and fluffy, the vadas crispy and golden, and the dosa—light, thin, and perfectly roasted. Each dish is accompanied by hot sambar and fresh coconut chutney that bring out authentic South Indian flavors.
One of the best parts of Mani’s is their warm and generous service. The staff pours unlimited sambar and chutney on your plate until you gently say “enough.” This simple yet heartfelt gesture has become the USP (Unique Selling Point) of the place. It's not just about the food, but the love and hospitality that comes with it.
Once I finish my meal, I always end with a cup of their aromatic filter coffee. Whether you prefer it light or strong, Mani’s coffee is brewed to perfection—rich, bold, and served in traditional steel tumblers that enhance its charm. For health-conscious guests like me, they also offer sugar-free tea, which is light, refreshing, and perfect to start the workday with clarity and balance.
After breakfast, I continue with my day feeling satisfied and refreshed. That peaceful moment at Mani’s sets a positive tone for whatever work lies ahead.
Mani’s Lunch Home is not just a restaurant for me. It’s a monthly ritual, a memory lane of flavors, and a place where time slows down—where every bite takes me back to the roots of comfort and tradition. In a fast-moving city like Mumbai, Mani’s is a calm, soulful corner that never changes.

featured_reviews.name: vru
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Udupi Shri Krishna Restaurant, which is conveniently located just a 1-minute walk from Matunga East Railway Station—making it extremely easy to reach without any hassle.

I learned that the restaurant was inaugurated by Sane Guruji, which adds a nice historical and cultural touch to the place.

When we arrived, we had to wait in the coupon queue, but it was quite smooth. Within about 10 minutes, our name was called. Considering it was a Saturday, the waiting time was very reasonable. I’ve heard that sometimes the wait can go up to 45 minutes to an hour, but we were lucky.

The staff at the counter was very polite and attentive. One thing that stood out was how they reminded everyone to wash their hands before eating—such a small yet thoughtful and caring gesture.

The food is served on a banana leaf, which adds a traditional and authentic feel. The entire meal felt fresh, simple, and very much like home-cooked food.

The thali included:

2 sabjis
1 koshimbir (cucumber salad)
Roti and puri
Curd
Pickle
Buttermilk
Nimbu rasam and regular rasam
Rice with ghee
One sweet (options like rasgulla, halwa, shrikhand, or gulab jamun)

Curd and sweets are limited, while the rest is unlimited.

The taste was excellent—especially the curd and nimbu rasam, which were absolutely delicious. The rasgulla we had was fresh, mildly sweet, and exceeded expectations.

The management and service were top-notch. The staff ensured that hot food was served in every round, which made the experience even better. Overall, it truly felt like having a comforting meal at home.

The full thali costs ₹300, and the mini thali is ₹200, which is quite reasonable for the quality and quantity offered.

My only suggestion would be to introduce a premium thali option at a slightly higher price, including a few more South Indian dishes for those who want to explore more variety.

Overall, a wonderful experience—highly recommended to everyone! 👍

featured_reviews.name: DV
featured_reviews.review_text: This is an iconic eatery that is as old as 84 years. It's is a true treasure for Mumbaikars who like South Indian vegetarian food. It serves a full unlimited meal from the south Indian cuisines with Tamil dishes being prominently cooked and served. It's traditionally served on a banana leaf making it visually appealing. The Thali as it is known has Rasam, Sambar, Dal, Rice with option of ghee atop, Poori, Chapati, 2 dry cooked vegetables and 2 gravy based vegetables. There is curd and flavoured (ginger/coriander) butter milk. There is a choice of dessert; my favourite is the Moong Dal payasam. At a modest 300/- bucks it's absolutely value for money. It's a living testament of cultural bonding between the South Indian community and the local Maharashtrians as well as Gujratis. The fact that it was inaugurated by Sane Guruji makes it even richer in identity.

An iconic South Indian cuisine restaurant in the iconic Matunga east neighbourhood of Mumbai. Everything, I repeat, every damn food item here is par excellence.

Things eaten: Paniyaram, Rassam, Medu Vada, Kanchipuram idli, appam with coconut stew, mysore onion dosa, cheese pav bhaji, pineapple sheera AND filter coffee.

Verdict: The Medu vada is truly one of the best I have ever had. It is so soft yet crispy at the same time. The coconut chutney and Tamilian sambar is unparalleled. Appam with coconut stew is amazing as well. Especially the stew was so delicious. Mysore onion dosa feels rich in flavour and is prepared in pure ghee. Kanchipuram idli was a decent one and a bit sour. Paniyaram was a one-of-a-kind and is a must try. Cheese pav bhaji was not bad but failed to meet the bar raised by other food items. For desserts, you have to have the pineapple sheera and you can thank me later. A south indian cuisines is incomplete with the iconic filter coffee and the coffee here will not disappoint you. The service is super quick and they serve you unlimited Sambar and Chutney

This restaurant was hitting home-runs after home-runs and I was about to give this place the coveted 5-star rating when they committed a hygienic blunder. I found a small hair in their Pav. Hygiene is as important as the taste and had they not compromised on the hygiene, my search for the 5-starred restaurant would have ended today. But alas the search continues!!

### Apoorva: A Hidden Gem for Delicious Vegetarian Delights

If you’re searching for a restaurant in Dadar that delivers more than just satisfying food, look no further than **Apoorva**. This pure veg family restaurant, nestled in the heart of Dadar, is a culinary haven for those who appreciate authentic Maharashtrian, South Indian, North Indian, and Desi Chinese cuisine—all served with a generous side of flavor and quality.

#### **Food Quality and Taste: A Delightful Surprise**
The moment you take your first bite at Apoorva, you’ll understand why it’s a local favorite. The food quality here is impeccable, from the freshest ingredients to the skilled preparation. Every dish, whether it’s the spicy Pav Bhaji, the creamy Butter Paneer  Masala, the crisp and savory Dosas, or the perfectly spiced Hakka Noodles, bursts with authentic flavors. The South Indian offerings, in particular, are a standout, with sambar that tastes like it’s straight out of a traditional kitchen and dosas that are golden, crispy, and oh-so-satisfying.

Apoorva has mastered the art of balancing taste with health, ensuring that the food is not just tasty but also light on the stomach, making it ideal for regular visits. Whether you’re a local or a visitor, the varied menu has something to please every palate.

Ambiance: Choices for Every Mood.
Apoorva offers three distinct seating options, catering to different preferences:
1. **Roadside Open Seats**: Perfect for those who enjoy dining al fresco, these seats give you a lively view of the bustling streets of Dadar. It's a great choice if you love people-watching while enjoying your meal. I love sitting here during Monsoon.
2. **Non-AC Inside Restaurant**: For a more traditional dining experience, the non-AC section offers a cozy, no-frills environment where you can focus on the food and conversation.
3. **AC Seats Inside Restaurant**: If you’re looking to beat the heat, the AC section provides a comfortable and cool respite from the Mumbai sun.

However, the seating area here can feel a bit cramped, so it’s best for smaller groups.

While the ambiance is simple and straightforward, it’s the food that truly shines at Apoorva. The seating might be cumbersome, especially during peak hours, but the culinary experience more than makes up for it.

**Parking: A Word of Caution**
One thing to note: if you’re planning to drive, parking can be a challenge. Roadside parking is notoriously difficult in this busy area, so it’s wise to avoid bringing a car if possible. Opt for public transport or a quick Taxi ride to save yourself the hassle.

**Location: A Convenient Spot in Dadar**
Apoorva’s location is another big plus. Situated close to major landmarks like Shivaji Park, Dadar Beach, Sushrusha Hospital, and Ranade Road, it’s easily accessible whether you’re out for a stroll, visiting a friend, or just exploring the neighborhood. Despite being in such a prime area, Apoorva maintains its reputation as one of the best budget-friendly restaurants around.

**Final Thoughts**
Apoorva is more than just a restaurant; it’s a place where food lovers come together to enjoy hearty, flavorful meals without breaking the bank. The quality, taste, and variety of the food make it a must-visit for anyone in Dadar, especially if you’re looking for a budget-friendly option that doesn’t compromise on flavor. Whether you’re in the mood for a quick snack or a full meal, Apoorva is ready to serve you with warmth and authenticity.

Next time you’re in Dadar, don’t miss the chance to dine at Apoorva—you’ll leave with a full stomach and a happy heart.
